reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows precipitation strengthening and delayed shear localization in Al-based eutectic/fcc HEAs with L12 and B2 phases, but none of the evidence involves the HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy, B2 precipitation in a BCC matrix, or the specific mechanism of coherent B2 precipitates enhancing dynamic strain hardening in refractory alloys. The key premises about the intervention's effect on this specific material are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Aging a refractory high-entropy alloy can produce nano-scale coherent B2 precipitates in a BCC matrix.
Nano-scale precipitates act as strong obstacles to dislocation motion, enhancing dynamic strain hardening.
Enhanced strain hardening delays adiabatic shear band formation and improves uniform deformation under dynamic loading.
The HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy can be aged to form a dual-phase BCC + B2 microstructure without embrittlement.
Precipitation strengthening observed in other HEAs translates to improved dynamic properties in this specific alloy.
